title: Why You Must Have High Behavior Standards For Online Lessons
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Writing during the shift to emergency remote learning, Linsin pushes back against the widespread instinct to lower behavior expectations in online classes just to keep attendance numbers up. He argues that easing standards backfires, ultimately reducing engagement rather than increasing it, because it strips away three things students need: purpose, pride, and personal discipline. Without high standards, he contends, students sense that online school is a lesser, less meaningful version of real school and disengage accordingly. He acknowledges that workload may reasonably be reduced given the circumstances, but insists behavior expectations should not follow suit. The piece ends with a call to build (or restore) a clear online classroom management plan with defined rules and consequences.
points: Argues that lowering behavior standards to boost online attendance actually causes fewer students to show up over time.
Identifies purpose, pride, and personal discipline as the three things students lose when standards are relaxed.
Distinguishes between reducing workload, which may be reasonable, and reducing behavior standards, which is not.
Contends that pride is an underused motivator that raising standards can activate in students.
Calls for building or restoring a written online classroom management plan with clear rules and consequences.
quotes: While I don’t dispute that we should shoot for high attendance rates, lowering behavior standards isn’t the way to do it.
When you lower the importance and seriousness—and sacredness—of learning and being in school, you remove from students a sense of purpose.
Simply raising behavior standards—or having behavior standards—lends a specialness and exclusivity to your online lessons.
It’s harder to realize the power inside each one of us to change our circumstances through determination and hard work and easier to point fingers and blame others for our predicaments.
Because of time and logistical constraints, the amount of work we ask of our students may need to be adjusted down a notch or two. But there is zero reason why behavior standards should follow suit.
Restore purpose, pride, and personal discipline, and your online lessons will matter to your students.
